# Benchmark session report

## Discoveries
- The challenge protocol requires frozen, independently keyed outcomes across correctness, grounding, and fidelity while retaining unsupported/native gaps; see [protocol](../benchmark/protocol.md#challenges).
- Public development inventories contain 11 cases with zero attempted or executed native validation and unavailable native references; see [case README](../benchmark/cases/dev/README.md).

## Status
Implemented the stdlib-only generator [challenges.py](../benchmark/scripts/challenges.py) and three public JSON fixtures plus [README](../benchmark/challenges/README.md). Fixtures cover positive controls, wrong answers and citations, omissions, false/true/unverified extras, duplicates, contradictions, constant export, empty/truncated/failed probes, unsupported cases, missing keys, and zero executed tests. Each records source case/revision, contract-shaped submissions, fixed denominators, expected dimension outcomes, and explicit ledgers/gaps.

The generator successfully produced all three fixtures without `LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT`; the requested `--check` was run after generation. No scorer, evaluator change, product code, challenge execution, readiness, threshold, or scope claim was made.

## Discoveries
- Native semantic keys, reader execution, independent review, and executable scoring remain unavailable; the VI fixture preserves these as unsupported rather than passing them.

## What next
A separate reviewer should inspect the generated fixtures against the protocol and independently check the provisional public inventories. A Policymaker may then order evaluator work; do not treat these public fixtures as withheld evaluation cases or as executed challenge results. Pinning and milestone status remain pending in the parallel preparation task.
